Marzipan Fruits

Served at: St. Nicholas Day

Makes about 2 dozen small fruitsPrep 45 min

Marzipan fruits are delightful, miniature confections made from almond paste, often beautifully colored and shaped to resemble various fruits. They are a traditional treat given on St. Nicholas Day, particularly in European cultures, where they symbolize the abundance and sweetness of the season and are often tucked into children's shoes or stockings as a sweet surprise from St. Nicholas.

Ingredients

  • 8 ounces (225 g) almond paste
  • 1 cup (120 g) powdered sugar, plus more for dusting
  • 1/2 teaspoon (2.5 ml) almond extract
  • Gel food coloring (red, green, yellow, orange, etc.)
  • Optional: Whole cloves (for stems), cocoa powder (for shading)

Method

  1. In a medium bowl, combine the almond paste, 1 cup (120 g) powdered sugar, and almond extract. If your almond paste is very firm, you can microwave it for 10-15 seconds to soften slightly before mixing.
  2. Knead the mixture by hand until it is smooth, pliable, and well combined. If the mixture is too sticky, add a little more powdered sugar, a teaspoon at a time, until it reaches a workable consistency.
  3. Divide the marzipan into several portions, depending on how many different fruit colors you wish to create.
  4. Add a small amount of gel food coloring to each portion. Knead each portion thoroughly until the color is evenly distributed and vibrant. Use red for apples or strawberries, green for pears or limes, yellow for bananas or lemons, and orange for oranges.
  5. Take small pieces of colored marzipan and shape them into miniature fruits. For example, roll red marzipan into small balls for apples, making a slight indentation on top and bottom, and inserting a whole clove for a stem. Shape orange marzipan into balls and gently press a textured surface (like a grater or fine sieve) onto them for a peel effect. Form yellow marzipan into curved logs for bananas, or green marzipan into teardrops for pears.
  6. For added realism, you can use a small, clean paintbrush to dust some fruits with a tiny amount of cocoa powder (e.g., for the 'blush' on an apple or the bottom of a pear).
  7. Place the finished marzipan fruits on a parchment-lined baking sheet or plate.
  8. Allow the marzipan fruits to air dry at room temperature for at least 2-3 hours, or preferably overnight. This will create a slight crust on the outside, helping them hold their shape and preventing stickiness.
  9. Arrange the dried marzipan fruits attractively on a platter for serving, or pack them into small decorative boxes as gifts for St. Nicholas Day.

Tips

  • Use high-quality almond paste for the best flavor and texture.
  • Gel food colorings provide vibrant colors without adding excess moisture to the marzipan, which can make it sticky.
  • Store finished marzipan fruits in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 weeks, or in the refrigerator for longer freshness.
